About Us 

Amity Care Services is a Mornington Peninsula based disability and home care support provider, founded by a team of registered nurses with extensive clinical experience in complex and acute care. We deliver Supported Independent Living, Specialist Disability Accommodation, Short Term Accommodation, Support Coordination, Psychosocial Recovery Coaching and clinical nursing services across the region, and can provide 24/7 support to our clients. Our values of loyalty, trust and honesty shape how we work with each other and the people we support. 

About the Role 

We are seeking a motivated and organised Rostering Coordinator to join our busy Rostering team at Amity Care Services. 

This role is responsible for coordinating accurate, timely and person-centred rosters for participants and support workers. You will work closely with the Rostering Lead, support workers, participants, families and internal departments to ensure shifts are filled appropriately, participant needs are met, and staffing arrangements remain compliant and sustainable. 

This is a fast-paced role suited to someone who enjoys problem-solving, communicating clearly, working under pressure, and supporting both staff and participants with professionalism and care. 

Key Responsibilities 

Coordinate and maintain participant and staff rosters in line with participant needs, staff availability and service requirements 

Allocate support workers to shifts, including new engagements, ongoing supports, respite and Supported Independent Living arrangements 

Respond to roster changes, cancellations, unfilled shifts and day-to-day staffing issues in a timely and professional manner 

Communicate clearly with support workers, participants, families, coordinators and internal teams regarding roster updates and changes 

Support smooth handovers for new participants, new staff, first shifts and meet and greets 

Monitor staff availability, shift allocations, travel considerations, skills matching and continuity of support 

Maintain accurate rostering records and documentation within VisualCare and related systems 

Escalate concerns regarding participant safety, staff conduct, availability gaps, compliance risks or service continuity to the Rostering Lead or relevant manager 

Work collaboratively with Recruitment, Clinical, Accounts and Management to support safe and consistent service delivery 

Ensure rostering practices align with Amity Care Services policies, NDIS requirements and SCHADS Award considerations 

About You 

We are looking for someone who is calm, organised and confident communicating with a wide range of people. You will be able to manage competing priorities, think quickly, and remain professional when dealing with last-minute changes or complex rostering issues. 

You will bring: 

Ability to work flexibly across a seven-day roster 

Experience in rostering, scheduling, administration or coordination, ideally within disability, aged care, home care or community services 

Strong communication and interpersonal skills 

Excellent attention to detail and time management 

Ability to work in a busy environment and manage competing priorities 

Confidence using computer systems, Microsoft Office and rostering or care management platforms such as VisualCare 

A practical problem-solving approach and the ability to remain calm under pressure 

A genuine interest in supporting vulnerable people in our community 

Understanding of confidentiality, professional boundaries and respectful communication 

Knowledge of the NDIS, SCHADS Award or community services sector would be highly regarded 

Requirements 

NDIS Worker Screening Check and Working with Children Check, or willingness to obtain 

Completed NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission Worker Orientation Module, or willingness to complete 

Current driver licence and reliable transport may be required depending on business needs 

Ability to work from our Mornington Peninsula office 

Why Join Amity? 

Be part of a values-driven, growing organisation making a genuine difference 

Work within a supportive and collaborative team environment 

Contribute to safe, reliable and person-centred supports for participants 

Opportunity to build your skills in rostering, coordination, NDIS service delivery and compliance 

Join an organisation that values loyalty, trust, honesty and continuous improvement 

How to Apply 

To apply, please submit a cover letter and current resume outlining your relevant experience, your interest in the Rostering Coordinator role, and what you believe you could bring to Amity Care Services to recruitment@amitycareservices.com.au.  

Applications close: 3rd August 2026 

For a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Taryn Brien 1800 426 489.

Full-time Wall and Floor Tiler position available with a competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Hurlstone Park, NSW 2193

•	Full-Time Position
•	$80,000 - $90,000 plus superannuation 
•	Operate within a professional setting.

FerMax Stone Pty Ltd is an Australian company established in 2012, specialising in the installation of premium wall and floor tiling, natural stone, porcelain and other high-quality surface finishes for residential and commercial projects. Since its establishment, the company has built a reputation for delivering quality workmanship, reliability and exceptional customer service across a wide range of projects.
On behalf of our client, we are looking for an experienced and skilled Wall and Floor tiler to join our team on a full-time basis

Position Responsibilities and Tasks

As a Wall and Floor Tiler, your duties will include, but will not be limited to:

•	Interpret plans and specifications; confirm measurements, quantities, layout lines and levels prior to commencing tiling works.
•	Measure, mark and set out surfaces using levelling equipment (including laser levels) to establish correct alignment, falls and datum lines.
•	Measure, cut, shape and install custom heritage mosaic tiles and decorative stone finishes, ensuring accurate pattern alignment, preserving heritage design features and delivering high-quality workmanship in accordance with project specifications.
•	Prepare wall and floor substrates by removing old tiles, grout and adhesives; filling holes and cracks; and cleaning/priming surfaces to ensure suitable adhesion and finish.
•	Lay and fix tiles (including ceramic, clay, slate, marble, glass and similar materials) to internal and external walls and floors to achieve required patterns, alignment and tolerances.
•	Apply adhesives and bedding materials to substrates and/or tile backs as required, ensuring correct coverage, bonding and curing in line with product specifications.
•	Cut, shape and fit tiles using hand and power tile-cutting tools to finish edges, corners and penetrations around fittings, pipes and fixtures.
•	Maintain consistent alignment and spacing throughout installation, checking for lippage, level, line and falls, and adjusting as required during installation.
•	Complete grouting, finishing and clean-down, including removing excess grout and presenting a consistent, defect-free surface finish.
•	Support waterproofing outcomes by assisting with waterproofing preparation/detailing and coordinating tiling works with waterproofing stages and inspection hold points, ensuring correct detailing at junctions and penetrations in wet areas and external areas.
•	Undertake substrate preparation activities that support tiling quality (e.g., grinding, levelling and surface preparation), and coordinate transitions/interfaces with epoxy or other protective floor finishes where required by project scope.
•	Work collaboratively on major construction sites across Sydney/NSW, liaising with site foremen and project managers regarding sequencing, access, quality inspections and program timeframes.
•	Maintain compliance with WHS requirements, including safe manual handling, correct PPE use, silica dust controls and safe operation of plant and tools used for cutting and surface preparation.


Qualifications and Skills:

•	Certificate III in Wall and Floor Tiling or relevant trade qualification.
•	At least two years of relevant experience.
•	Sound knowledge of wall and floor tiling techniques and installation methods.
•	Experience working with ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite and natural stone products.
•	Ability to read and interpret plans and technical drawings.
•	Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality workmanship.

Salary:
The role offers a remuneration package of $80,000 - $90,000 per annum, plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

About the Department - Program






The CY-HOPE team provides wellbeing-psychosocial support, peer support and brief clinical support to young people in the 0-18 age range presenting with suicide and self-harm concerns. The Wellbeing Support Worker will work as part of the CY-HOPE team under its governance and support and, as such, will have opportunities to work in a variety of community settings.







About the Team






The Infant, Child and Youth Area Mental Health & Wellbeing Service provides assessment and treatment for infants, children, adolescents, young people and their families. We work with the 0-18 age in the Southern Region. We provide a comprehensive assessment service and a range of treatment options including inpatient treatment in times of crisis, community (outpatient) treatment, group programs, family therapy, and specialist services.






The Child & Youth Hospital Outreach Post-Suicidal Engagement (CY-HOPE) Team is a core component of Victoria's suicide prevention framework, which aimed to halve Victoria's suicide rate by 2025. This new service gives children and young people who are intentionally self-harming, experiencing suicidal ideation, or have attempted suicide a rapid and intensive form of support that is designed to prevent rate of recurrence and ultimately reduce rates of suicide among children and young people. Importantly, this includes engagement and support of their parents-carers, families and extended support networks in assertive outreach provided.






All stakeholders (children, young people, their parents-carers, families and service providers) will work together in this Child and Youth HOPE service at the Infant, Child and Youth Area Mental Health & Wellbeing Service at Monash Health. This service has been co-designed with and for young people and carers, First Nations people, people from Culturally Diverse Communities, LGBTIQ+ people, people in Out of Home Care, and Neurodivergent people.

The Wellbeing Support Workers are the key workers for the young people in the CY-HOPE Team. They carry a caseload of 10 young people and provide non-clinical psychosocial support to young people and their families. This may include:









supporting engaging with friends, family, school, community programs












developing independent life skills












liaising with and supporting referrals to other mental health supports and-or family support services.












A combination of clinic based and outreach appointments









They work alongside the mental health clinicians, peer workers and consultant psychiatrist in the CY-HOPE Team to provide a meaningful approach to care that assists the young person to stay safe and connect with essential services in the first 12 weeks following discharge from hospital or contact with the service after a suicide attempt or a suicidal crisis.






The 0.8 EFT position will require you to work on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, with the other day to be of your choosing.







About You

Care I Wish, located in Scoresby, VIC, is a trusted provider of personalised care services, dedicated to supporting people living with disabilities, the elderly, and individuals with complex needs. With a mission to uphold the dignity, independence, and wellbeing of every client, Care I Wish offers a wide range of services under the NDIS framework, including in-home support, community access, personal care, and specialised care services. Our approach is built on compassion, empowerment, and tailoring every service to suit everyone’s goals and lifestyle. We are currently seeking a compassionate, reliable, and experienced Aged or Disabled Carer to join our growing team. This is a full-time opportunity (38 hours per week), ideal for someone passionate about providing person-centred care in a home and community setting.

Job Position: Aged or Disabled Carer

Location: Scoresby, VIC

Key Responsibilities:
•	Support clients with daily living activities, including personal hygiene, bathing, grooming, and dressing.
•	Assist individuals with mobility and physical transfers, including the use of mobility aids, ensuring their safety and comfort.
•	Prepare and serve nutritious meals in line with dietary needs and preferences, and support with feeding where necessary.
•	Provide emotional support and companionship, fostering meaningful connections to combat isolation and build trust.
•	Facilitate and encourage participation in social outings and community activities, aligned with clients’ interests and goals.
•	Assist with household tasks such as vacuuming, laundry, dusting, mopping, and maintaining a clean and safe living environment.
•	Support clients in shopping, medication reminders, and attending medical or personal appointments. Help develop and maintain daily routines and promote independence wherever possible.
•	Support participants with NDIS plans, implementing scheduled activities and reporting on progress and changes in condition.
•	Participate in care planning meetings, work collaboratively with allied health professionals, and communicate effectively with clients’ families or guardians.
•	Promote and protect the dignity, privacy, and confidentiality of all clients always. Be adaptable to different environments, including live-in arrangements if required.
•	Maintain accurate documentation and reports related to care activities and incident management.

Offer: Full-Time (38 Hours Per Week) with Salary $75,000–$85,000 + Superannuation

Skills & Qualifications Required:
•	A minimum of 1 year of experience in a similar role within disability or aged care support.
•	Possess an AQF Certificate II or III in Aged Care, Individual Support, Disability, or a relevant field.

Personal Attributes:
•	Empathetic, caring, and respectful
•	Reliable, punctual, and responsible
•	Strong interpersonal and communication skills

At Care I Wish, we value people who go the extra mile to ensure each client receives not just care, but connection, empowerment, and joy. If you’re passionate about helping others live with dignity and independence, we would love to hear from you.
